input_signals.name: Cash-Scarcity Gross Profit Inflection
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross-profit improvement predicts higher returns, and deterioration predicts lower returns, with both effects strongest among cash-depleted firms.
input_signals.reasoning: When cash reserves are low, the direction of core operating profitability is more consequential for survival and external-financing needs. The signed trend distinguishes genuine operating turnarounds from continued deterioration without relying on a static solvency ratio or binary distress state.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 3 ), 1 ), rank( neg( ratio( che, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Unshielded Tax Exhaustion
input_signals.hypothesis: Tax expense near its historical low predicts lower returns when depreciation is also near its historical low, indicating that tax exhaustion is unlikely to be explained by noncash depreciation shields.
input_signals.reasoning: The depreciation leg changes the interpretation of low tax expense rather than adding another same-direction profitability proxy: low taxes accompanied by high depreciation can be benign, while low taxes without that shield more plausibly indicate taxable losses. Own-history positions and within-industry ranks reduce scale and industry effects without relying on profitability levels likely to be absorbed by RMW.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( txt, at ), 5 ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Tax-Exhausted Cost Instability
input_signals.hypothesis: Instability in the gross cost share predicts lower returns most strongly when tax expense is near the bottom of the firm's own history.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the archived gross-profit-trend and cash-scarcity pairing with an operating-risk amplification mechanism: input-cost instability is more dangerous when tax exhaustion indicates weak taxable profitability. The continuous volatility and historical-tax ranks avoid binary conditioning and do not reuse the prior cash modifier.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( vol( ratio( cogs, revt ), 5 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( txt, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Revenue Trend Under Thin Operating Runway
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-productivity improvement predicts higher returns, and deterioration predicts lower returns, with both effects strongest when cash provides little operating-cost coverage.
input_signals.reasoning: Cumulative revenue downside under a thin operating runway generated strong portfolio alpha but an essentially flat cross-sectional slope, suggesting a tail-only score. Replacing downside accumulation with a signed revenue trend should produce a more monotonic relation while preserving the demand-survival mechanism and continuous runway conditioning.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( trend( ratio( revt, at ), 3 ), 1 ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( che, ma( cogs, 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Asymmetric Revenue Resilience
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUB(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(revt, at), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(NEG(TS_SUM(MUL(DELTA(RATIO(revt, at), 1), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(revt, at), 1)), 0)), 5)), 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(che, MA(cogs, 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue improvement net of accumulated downside shocks predicts higher returns most strongly when operating cash runway is thin.
input_signals.reasoning: Signed revenue trend produced joint cross-sectional and portfolio evidence, while downside accumulation produced stronger tail alpha but a flat slope. Subtracting the downside rank from the trend rank creates a scale-robust path-quality measure that distinguishes smooth recovery from improvement punctuated by severe contractions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sub( ind_rank( trend( ratio( revt, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( neg( ts_sum( mul( delta( ratio( revt, at ), 1 ), indicator( neg( delta( ratio( revt, at ), 1 ) ), 0 ) ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( che, ma( cogs, 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Recovery After Cash-Earnings Losses
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 3), 1), IND_RANK(WINSOR(NEG(TS_SUM(MUL(RATIO(ADD(pi, dp), at), INDICATOR(NEG(ADD(pi, dp)), 0)), 5)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross-profit improvement predicts higher returns, and deterioration predicts lower returns, most strongly after severe cumulative pre-depreciation earnings losses.
input_signals.reasoning: Cumulative cash-earnings losses generated reliable portfolio alpha but only weak slope evidence because the all-positive severity score mainly isolated a distressed tail. A signed operating trend sorts recoveries from continued deterioration within that high-loss state, potentially adding monotonic cross-sectional information without discarding the tail mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 3 ), 1 ), ind_rank( winsor( neg( ts_sum( mul( ratio( add( pi, dp ), at ), indicator( neg( add( pi, dp ) ), 0 ) ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidity-Backed Recovery After Cash Losses
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 3), 1), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(NEG(TS_SUM(MUL(RATIO(ADD(pi, dp), at), INDICATOR(NEG(ADD(pi, dp)), 0)), 5)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, lct))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross-profit recovery after cumulative pre-depreciation earnings losses predicts higher returns when current liquidity is sufficient to fund the turnaround.
input_signals.reasoning: Gross recovery after cash-like losses produced a strong slope but negligible portfolio alpha, suggesting that illiquid turnaround firms contaminated the high-signal tail. Cash coverage acts as survival validation: historical loss severity makes the recovery economically important, while liquidity makes it financeable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 3 ), 1 ), mul( ind_rank( winsor( neg( ts_sum( mul( ratio( add( pi, dp ), at ), indicator( neg( add( pi, dp ) ), 0 ) ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( che, lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Demand-Contraction Working-Capital Overhang
input_signals.hypothesis: A large working-capital stock relative to the operating cost base predicts lower returns when revenue productivity is deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: Working capital can represent useful liquidity in normal conditions but becomes an overhang when falling demand leaves inventories or receivables stranded. The interaction uses a balance-sheet stock rather than the Sloan working-capital change and abandons the unsupported depreciation-based fixed-cost interpretation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( wcap, ma( cogs, 3 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( revt, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Rank-Balanced Dual Operating Recovery
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(MIN(ZSCORE(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(revt, at), 3))), ZSCORE(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 3)))), 1), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(che, MA(cogs, 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating recovery predicts higher returns under thin cash runway only when both revenue productivity and gross profitability improve on a standardized basis.
input_signals.reasoning: Cross-sectional rank standardization puts revenue and gross-profit trends on comparable scales before applying the minimum, preventing gross-profit trend from mechanically binding. The weaker standardized recovery channel determines the signal, so sales growth without margin-adjusted improvement cannot qualify as a strong turnaround.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( min( zscore( ind_rank( trend( ratio( revt, at ), 3 ) ) ), zscore( ind_rank( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 3 ) ) ) ), 1 ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( che, ma( cogs, 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Revenue Recovery in Unshielded Tax Distress
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(revt, at), 3), 1), MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(txt, at), 5))), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-productivity improvement predicts higher returns, and deterioration predicts lower returns, among firms with both tax expense and depreciation near historical lows.
input_signals.reasoning: The joint tax-and-depreciation trough produced reliable negative distress evidence, while revenue trend under constrained states generated strong positive recovery evidence. The signed trend orders firms within this proven distress state, distinguishing operating revival from continued contraction rather than merely re-encoding the trough.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( trend( ratio( revt, at ), 3 ), 1 ), mul( ind_rank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( txt, at ), 5 ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ) ) ) )
